chunks: 2366 - Al-Naḍr narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying:

Regarding the pigeons of Makkah: the domesticated bird is from the pigeons of the Haram. Whoever slaughters a bird from them, then he must give in charity something better than its price; and if he was in ihram, then one sheep is due for each bird.

key_terms.الطَّيْرُ الْأَهْلِيُّ: the domesticated bird, counted here among the birds of the Haram
key_terms.حَمَامِ الْحَرَمِ: the pigeons of the Sacred Sanctuary
key_terms.حَمَامِ مَكَّةَ: the pigeons of Makkah, which are accorded protected status here
key_terms.شَاةٌ: a sheep due as expiatory compensation
key_terms.مُحْرِمًا: being in the state of ihram during hajj or ʿumrah

ai.seo_question: What is the kaffarah for slaughtering a bird from the pigeons of the Haram while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the birds of Makkah and the Haram, treating even domesticated birds among them as protected. It states that slaughtering such a bird requires compensation through charity greater than its price, and if the person is in ihram, the penalty becomes one sheep per bird.
